The shot wounded the animal but didn't kill it.
Careless words can wound worse than insults.

senses.head: To hurt someone's feelings deeply
examples: That remark wounded her more than he realized.
Criticism like that can wound a young writer.
He looked genuinely wounded by the question.

entries.meaning: To hurt a person or animal so that part of the body is damaged. ---
examples: Six passengers were injured in the crash.
He injured his shoulder lifting boxes all afternoon.
Bad shoes will injure your knees over time.

entries.meaning: To cause damage or injury to a person, an animal, or a thing. ---
examples: The runoff harms the fish downstream.

entries.meaning: To injure skin or fruit so that a dark mark appears without the surface breaking. ---
examples: She bruised her elbow on the door frame.
Peaches bruise if you stack them three deep.
His arm was badly bruised from the fall.
entries.contrast: Ends in a z sound: BROOZ, not "broos".

entries.meaning: To injure a joint by twisting it suddenly. ---
examples: I sprained my wrist playing volleyball.
You can sprain an ankle just stepping off a curb.
He has been walking on a sprained knee for a week.

entries.meaning: Fracture has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She fractured her wrist in the fall.

The X-ray showed a fractured rib.

examples: His enthusiasm infected the whole team.

entries.meaning: To become healthy again after an injury, or to make someone healthy again. ---

entries.meaning: Cure has 2 distinct senses.

entries.meaning: To wrap cloth around an injured part of the body. ---

entries.meaning: To save something usable from a wreck, a fire, or a failing situation. ---

entries.meaning: To keep something in good condition so that it is not damaged or lost. ---

examples: The road deteriorated badly after two hard winters.

senses.head: To break down or lose quality over time, or to cause that to happen
examples: Sunlight degrades cheap plastic in a single season.

entries.meaning: To become worse, or to make something worse. ---
examples: The leak worsened overnight.

entries.contrast: The y stays after a vowel: decayed, decaying — compare carry → carried.

entries.meaning: To destroy metal slowly by chemical action. ---

examples: The gate rusted through in five years.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (salt rusts the frame), intransitive (the gate rusted)
